name: Jihadism
summary: Jihadism is the militant Islamist current that holds armed struggle to be a duty and the proper means of overthrowing regimes it judges un-Islamic and founding states, ultimately a caliphate, ruled by a literal sharia. It rejects democracy, nationalism and man-made law on the principle of God's sovereignty, and it permits declaring other Muslims apostates (takfir). Its mainstream, Salafi jihadism, treats the defence of Muslim lands as an individual obligation and targets the West and its allied Muslim rulers.
scope: The Salafi-jihadist mainstream of al-Qaeda and later the Islamic State, drawing on Sayyid Qutb, Abdullah Azzam and Osama bin Laden. It excludes nationalist or regional resistance groups such as Hezbollah or Hamas, which scholars distinguish from global jihadism, and quietist or political Salafism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Jihadist texts set out no health policy; adherents could back state provision as Islamic welfare or leave it to charity, so the answer is a genuine split inferred from general Islamist practice.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The sources discuss no wage policy and the ideology is indifferent to labour-market regulation beyond sharia, so this is an uninformed neutral.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Al Rasheed's description of the movement's economic outlook as broadly free-market is the only evidence, and it is not a developed doctrine.

public-ownership.rationale: Bin Laden complains that oil wealth is plundered by outsiders but never argues for state ownership of industry, so no side can be inferred.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Jihadists treat zakat as the lawful levy on wealth and man-made tax systems as illegitimate, so a call for much higher state taxation on the rich does not fit.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are a secular class organisation outside the sharia framework, so adherents would be cool toward them, though no source addresses them.

property-fundamental.rationale: Sharia protects property, but it can be overridden by religious duty and by hudud and jihad, so adherents would agree only moderately.

regulate-corporations.rationale: No source speaks to corporate regulation; sharia commercial rules could justify it but adherents have not taken a position.

cut-welfare.rationale: Almsgiving and care for the poor are religious duties, so adherents would resist describing welfare as harmful dependency, though they do not endorse state programmes as such.

worker-ownership.rationale: Worker ownership is a socialist idea that Islamist revivalists such as Qutb set against Islam, so it is inferred as disfavoured.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Jihadists regard the counter-terrorism label as a pretext of the Crusader-Zionist alliance, so they would not accept surveillance justified by it.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The movement seeks an uncompromising form of sharia, under which intoxicants are forbidden and punished.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents want blasphemy limited but also want freedom to denounce others by takfir, so the answer splits on what counts as hate speech.

strong-leader.rationale: Azzam holds that fighters choose a single amir and that the imam commands jihad, and groups bind themselves by a personal oath of allegiance, so unified strong command is favoured.

state-harmful.rationale: Jihadists want to build a state under Islamic law, a caliphate, so they reject the claim that the state is unnecessary.

limit-guns.rationale: Bin Laden calls for guerrilla war fought by the nation's sons, so an armed population is assumed; this is inferred, not stated as a gun policy.

empower-police-military.rationale: They want strong forces under Islamic rule but denounce the existing regimes' forces as tools of the West, so adherents split on funding existing ones.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Sex outside marriage is forbidden under the literalist sharia the movement demands, and its punishments are part of the programme.

decide-locally.rationale: Azzam seeks to unify divided authorities into one caliphate by jihad, so power should be central and unified rather than local.

rehabilitation.rationale: Jihadists apply hudud corporal and capital punishments, which favour retribution over rehabilitation.

traditional-family.rationale: The literalist movement upholds male-led families and distinct gender roles, and it condemns Western gender norms.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: It is incompatible with the uncompromising literal sharia the movement demands, though the sources do not discuss it directly.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the literalist sharia that jihadists adopt, under which abortion is largely prohibited; the sources do not discuss it.

more-religion-public.rationale: Jihadists aim to found states on Islamic principles and see Muslim societies' departure from sharia as ignorance (jahiliyyah) that must be reversed.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Jihadist ideology is framed by faith, not race, and it offers no stance on redress for historical racial injustices.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Literalist readings treat gender roles as divinely fixed, and jihadist ideologues condemn Western gender norms such as those Qutb attacked.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Jihadists reject nationalism in favour of a transnational umma, though they would preserve Islamic traditions, so they only weakly oppose this national framing.

gradual-change.rationale: Jihadism holds that armed struggle is the means to overturn existing regimes, which it denounces as un-Islamic, rather than respecting established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The sources do not address migration policy, and Muslim migration is valued while non-Muslim migration into Muslim lands is not, so the answer is split.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Bodies like the UN rest on man-made law, which jihadists reject on the principle of God's sovereignty (hakimiyya).

free-trade.rationale: The movement has no developed trade doctrine, only a reported free-market leaning, so the answer is a neutral inference.

nation-first.rationale: Jihadism rejects nationalism and works across borders, though it also rejects cooperation with Western-led global institutions, so the rejection is mild.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Foreign military intervention in Muslim lands is the grievance behind the jihad, and the 1998 fatwa casts Western forces as aggressors, not protectors.

open-borders.rationale: Jihadists want to erase borders among Muslim lands but not open them to non-Muslims, so there is no clean answer.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmental limits are not discussed in jihadist sources, and the ideology is indifferent to growth as such.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The sources do not take up climate policy, and it is not a concern of the movement.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Qutb's critique of modern materialist societies as jahiliyyah suggests scepticism of salvation by technology, though the movement uses technology for its ends.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear energy is not addressed in the jihadist literature, so no position follows from principles.

revolution-justified.rationale: Jihadism is defined as the view that armed confrontation is a legitimate and effective way to bring political change toward Islamic government.

experts-over-public.rationale: Jihadists place authority in God's law and distrust the traditional ulama, so neither experts nor the public are given the final say.

central-planning.rationale: Revivalists like Qutb present Islam as a third way apart from communism, so central planning is inferred as disfavoured.

socialized-markets.rationale: Market socialism is not discussed, and its secular framing would make it unattractive to adherents.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; the lawful levies in the sharia framework are zakat and Islamic taxes, so a land tax replacing others is unlikely to be endorsed.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Sharia prescribes fixed inheritance shares, so heavy state taxation of estates conflicts with a literalist reading; the sources do not address it.

basic-income.rationale: Unconditional state payments are not in jihadist doctrine, which places relief in zakat and charity.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Bin Laden attacks outside plunder of Muslim wealth but does not advance a tariff policy.

state-directs-investment.rationale: No stated position; resource sovereignty concerns appear but no industrial policy.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses the distribution of property, so adherents are indifferent.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Jihadists reject Marxist abolition of wages and money, and Islamic commerce assumes both; this is inferred.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Jihadist sources do not address monetary institutions, and adherents might favour a gold currency without having a settled view.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-run wage bargaining bodies are a secular corporatist design absent from jihadist thought.

one-party-rule.rationale: Salafi jihadists treat parties as divisive, though they accept a single leading movement under an amir, so they only mildly reject a ruling party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Bin Laden attacks the Saudi royal house as illegitimate, and the caliphate model they pursue rests on oath-of-allegiance, not hereditary right.

democracy-best.rationale: Salafi jihadists reject democracy because they see it as contradicting God's sovereignty (hakimiyya).

direct-votes.rationale: Popular lawmaking by vote contradicts God's sole right to legislate that the movement insists on.

workers-councils.rationale: Jihadists reject all popular-sovereignty bodies and secular class politics in favour of sharia rule.

right-to-secede.rationale: Azzam wants divided Muslim authorities united, so breaking states up is not a goal, though secession from regimes it deems apostate is acceptable.

natural-rulers.rationale: Authority belongs to the pious and the learned in Islamic tradition and to the amir chosen from among the mujahideen, which is a weak form of this claim.

political-violence-never.rationale: Jihadism holds armed struggle to be a duty and a legitimate method of political change.

war-builds-character.rationale: Azzam presents jihad as a duty whose neglect is a sin and that renews the community, which fits the claim loosely.

separate-church-state.rationale: Jihadists want states founded on Islamic principles, and Qutb called societies that follow man-made law ignorant.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The ideology seeks to restore Islamic law over man-made law in its most literal sense.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Sharia courts and an armed community under an amir are public religious authority, so privatising them is alien.

military-superiority.rationale: Azzam calls on the imam to send armies into enemy land regularly, implying a strong state, but the sources do not discuss superiority over rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Jihadism pursues a jihad across national boundaries and a community defined by faith, not by ethnicity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Jihadists see history as a struggle between Islam and ignorance, not between classes.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Inferred: Islamic law treats property and inheritance unequally and has no programme of levelling outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The sources do not address indigenous peoples, and religion, not indigeneity, frames the movement's claims to land.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Bin Laden complains of Western plunder of Muslim wealth, which suggests agreement in principle, though reparations are not a demand.

civilizational-union.rationale: Azzam argues jihad should reform the divided Muslim authorities toward one caliphate, and the movement aims to unite the Muslim world under Islamic law.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The ideology puts religious duty and sacrifice above self-interest, though it does not discuss self-interest as a moral doctrine.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Azzam frames jihad as a duty that overrides permission from parents, spouses and creditors, which puts religious duty ahead of personal claims.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed; Islamic teaching treats nature as creation, which gives no clear answer to intrinsic value.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; a movement that wants more fighters and a larger umma is unlikely to back population limits.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Qutb condemned modern materialist civilization morally, but jihadists do not oppose industry itself, so adherents split.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Jihadists use modern technology but see modern society as ignorance, so disrupting institutions for tech's sake is unattractive.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from literalist views on creation and the body; not discussed in sources.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Rule by algorithms conflicts with rule by God's law applied by rulers, which is inferred and not stated.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred: a clandestine movement benefits from private communications, though the sources do not discuss encryption.

restore-past-order.rationale: Jihadists take the early caliphs as the model and aim to restore Islamic rule rather than pursue modern progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Jihadists insist on literal adherence to scripture over pragmatic outcomes.

direct-action.rationale: Jihadists reject elections and parliaments, which they regard as man-made, and pursue change by armed struggle.

means-match-ends.rationale: Adherents claim their means are Islamic, but this is not a stated principle, and critics note the violence contradicts the ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Nothing suggests rejecting settled life; the movement wants a state and caliphate.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A Marxist idea with no place in the jihadist outlook, and the movement is organised by functions such as amirs, scholars and fighters.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Islam stresses charity for the needy but not a communist distribution principle.

production-for-use.rationale: A socialist formula with no presence in jihadist texts.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Islamic commerce permits profit, and the movement's complaints concern foreign plunder, not wage exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Jihadists reject class rule; sovereignty belongs to God.

collective-farming.rationale: No jihadist programme for collectivisation, and Islamic law protects private holding.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Bin Laden blames the Crusader-Zionist alliance, a religious not an economic structure, for aggression.

taxation-theft.rationale: Jihadists reject man-made taxes as illegitimate but accept zakat and Islamic levies, so only partly agree.

harm-principle.rationale: The literalist sharia the movement demands criminalises acts, such as apostasy and sexual offences, that harm no one else.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights and duties derive from God's law and the community, and the movement rejects equal rights across belief.

conscription.rationale: Azzam's fard ayn doctrine makes fighting compulsory for all Muslims nearby, but he does not discuss state conscription.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The ideology treats leaving the Muslim community as apostasy, not as a freedom.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred: the state is a religious institution, not a service business.

positive-liberty.rationale: The ideology defines freedom as submission to God, so a material-means conception is not its emphasis.

media-academia-power.rationale: Jihadists criticise Western media and education, but the sources do not present this specific claim.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Faith, not race, defines the community in jihadist thought; the claim is not discussed.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation by oath of allegiance to a leader is the model, not guild or family bodies.

total-state.rationale: Hakimiyya puts every area of life under God's law, which in practice means religious rule over culture, education and economy.

national-rebirth.rationale: Qutb described a society fallen into ignorance needing radical renewal, but the unit is the Muslim community, not the nation.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Azzam holds that offensive jihad is a collective duty for the imam to launch yearly, and the movement seeks a global caliphate.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Groups bind members and followers through a formal oath of allegiance (bay'ah) to a leader.

bound-labor.rationale: Not part of jihadist doctrine, which has no programme for serfdom.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Jihadists hold that truth is revealed and fixed, not power-relative, though Qutb treats secular knowledge as shaped by ignorance.

universal-morality.rationale: Moral truth is held to be universal but known by revelation rather than reason, so agreement is partial.

single-common-good.rationale: Hakimiyya holds that God's law fixes one good for all, so politics balancing competing interests is rejected.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Azzam treats Palestine as Muslim land to be defended by jihad, and the 1998 fatwa calls for forces to leave Muslim lands and attacks the Zionist alliance.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Jihadists support Palestinian return but oppose Jewish return, so the generic claim splits them.

revive-national-language.rationale: The sources do not address language policy; Arabic has religious status but isn't a national revival cause.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Democratic control as a principle is rejected by jihadists, and it is inferred to extend to firms.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; adherents want religious education but have no view on funding mechanisms.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not part of jihadist thought.

economic-freedom.rationale: Only a reported free-market tendency is documented, with no doctrine linking it to political freedom, which they reject anyway.

rule-by-example.rationale: The early caliphs are held up as the model of rule, though jihadists also rely heavily on punishment.

national-self-determination.rationale: The movement rejects nation-states in favour of a transnational caliphate, though it supports Muslim peoples fighting occupation.

force-without-un.rationale: Jihadists deny the UN any authority, and the 1998 fatwa calls for force by individuals without any international sanction.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Adherents follow sacred texts in their most literal sense, not reason as the sole guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; adherents might favour Muslims over others rather than citizens over immigrants.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Jihadist literature never discusses welfare conditionality; zakat goes to the needy by religious rule, so no work requirement can be inferred either way.

class-collaboration.rationale: Islamist revivalists reject class conflict, so cooperation is the inferred default.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Islamic State-style groups destroy heritage they see as idolatry, but not to make way for new creation, so only mild disagreement is inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: The 1998 fatwa calls on Muslims everywhere to fight the Western powers dominating Muslim lands and their allies.

workers-nation.rationale: The movement rejects both class and national organisation in favour of a faith community.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The movement's gender doctrine is described as discriminatory against women, with distinct roles written into law.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury is forbidden in the literal sharia the movement demands, though sources do not discuss it directly.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The community is defined by faith, not race; racial classification is not part of jihadist law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Jihadists see the state as God's instrument under right rule or as apostate regimes, not as a class instrument.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Bin Laden treats Gulf oil as the Muslims' largest asset, so adherents would favour exploiting it for themselves.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Adherents would not want Muslim migrants to give up their religion, but in a caliphate would expect non-Muslims to conform, so they split.

elite-replacement.rationale: Jihadists blame Zionist-crusader schemes, but the specific replacement conspiracy is a Western far-right theory they do not share.

proportional-representation.rationale: Elections and parliaments are rejected as man-made, so proportional allocation of seats is rejected too.

national-mission.rationale: The movement aims to extend Islamic rule worldwide, but the vehicle is the umma, not a particular country.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Jihadists defend male authority as divinely ordered and would not call it systematic advantage.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Bin Laden accuses the Saudi rulers of corruption and subservience to the US, and jihadists denounce Arab regimes as apostate.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred from Islamic teaching on the sanctity of life and marriage; not discussed.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The movement denounces regime abuses, so accountability of those forces would be welcome, though not for jihadists' own acts.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state is meant to enforce a total religious order, not be minimal.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Islam does not distinguish by race in marriage, so discouragement would conflict with the community's own teachings.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The movement splits true from false believers and treats people unequally on religious grounds.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist debate with no bearing on the jihadist outlook.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Jihadists see Israel as an alien implant in Muslim land, and the fatwa speaks of Zionist-crusader aggression, though settler-colonial vocabulary is not theirs.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Sharia personal law differs by religion and men and women, so a uniform code is contrary to the programme.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Leaving Islam is punishable by death, and conversion away from Islam is prohibited, so restriction is endorsed.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A Hindu-derived rule with no Islamic basis, and slaughter of cattle is permitted in Islam.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Jihadists want Islamic law and religious instruction to govern public institutions.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist thesis not applicable to the jihadist outlook.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Popular sovereignty is rejected, though rulers are installed by oath of allegiance, so consent matters only within God's law.

population-transfer.rationale: Jihadist groups have expelled minority communities they treated as unbelievers, though this is not stated as doctrine in the sources opened.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Azzam holds that offensive jihad is a collective duty of the state, so initiating force for the faith is permitted.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The movement sees history as a religious struggle but not as progress through competition.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Inferred: a regime under sharia would outlaw parties seeking to abolish it, as it already does apostasy.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican concept that is not discussed; adherents see freedom as submission to God alone.

separated-powers.rationale: The movement vests authority in the amir who applies God's law, not in checks among bodies.

vanguard-party.rationale: Qutb's vanguard of believers parallels the idea, but this statement concerns the working class and a party, so agreement is partial.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Care for the poor is a religious duty, but the movement's priorities are jihad and sharia.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public housing tenure is a Western policy question that jihadist texts never touch, so adherents have no position to infer.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Not addressed; jihadists are not concerned with industrial relations.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Provision is held to come from God, so blaming numbers for poverty is not natural for adherents.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The movement values a community of true believers and treats others unequally, which leans toward homogeneity, though the sources discuss religion, not ethnicity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Chance appointment conflicts with oath-bound or scholarly selection of leaders.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Jihadist states in wartime use summary executions and suspend protections, as the reported mass executions in ISIS territory show.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Classical Islamic jurisprudence mostly discourages price-fixing, so adherents lean against, though this is inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Inferred: a literalist regime would control media content, though the party form is not their model.

party-commands-army.rationale: The armed forces are commanded by amirs, not parties, so the framing does not fit.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Not addressed; membership turns on faith, not residence.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay for elected representatives presupposes parliaments that jihadists reject, and no source discusses officials' salaries.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Obedience to a leader by oath of allegiance resembles binding discipline, though the party form isn't theirs.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: A secular supranational union such as the EU rests on man-made law, though pooling sovereignty in a caliphate would be welcome.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The amir or imam commands the army and sends it into the field, per Azzam, and the caliph chooses the government.

church-by-bishops.rationale: An episcopal Christian question with no bearing on Sunni jihadist thought.

clerical-rule.rationale: Jihadists distrust the traditional ulama, yet value scholars and rule by the learned, so adherents split.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Marxist stance foreign to jihadists, who would instead support the Muslim side.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Literalist sharia rule restricts art and entertainment seen as immoral.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: A caliph or amir rules without term limits under a lifelong oath, though no source states it.

recall-officials.rationale: Allegiance is conditional on obedience to sharia, so rulers who break it may be removed, although not by voters.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Bin Laden demands US forces leave Muslim lands, and jihadists oppose alliances with non-Muslim powers.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Islamic law permits renting, so a ban is out of line.

people-in-arms.rationale: Bin Laden's 1996 declaration calls for guerrilla war fought by the nation's sons instead of the regular forces.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Azzam seeks to reunite divided Muslim authorities, and the movement rejects borders imposed on the Muslim world, though the sources do not name them.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed; jihadists criticise secular education but also prize religious scholarship.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Qutb described societies outside Islamic law as ignorance, ranking them below Islam.

death-penalty.rationale: Hudud and the death penalty for apostasy and for other offences are part of the sharia the movement seeks.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Gender equality and sex education are Western norms that the movement rejects.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Literalist reading of scripture favours creation teaching, though evolution is not discussed in the sources.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Strict sharia morality forbids it, so legal restriction is endorsed.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Membership in the umma is by faith and not by descent or birth place.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language is secondary to faith, and the movement is not concerned with minority languages.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Non-Muslims would not be exempt from sharia in a jihadist state, though Muslim minorities elsewhere may claim practice rights.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Conformity to a literal religious code is enforced, so eccentric living is discouraged.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Bin Laden complains of Western exploitation of Muslim wealth and riba is forbidden, which fits cancellation, though no source states it.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The 1998 fatwa links occupation to plunder of Muslim riches, suggesting political independence demands control of resources.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Writing a constitution by elected assembly is democratic lawmaking that the movement rejects in favour of sharia.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Economic development is not a stated priority; adherents would restrict freedoms for religion's sake.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not discussed; zakat is a duty among Muslims but jihadists oppose Western influence.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred from the defence of Muslim lands and independence from the West; sources do not discuss nuclear weapons.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Rulers are chosen by oath of allegiance, not by popular elections that jihadists regard as man-made.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Azzam holds that any Muslim land taken by unbelievers must be fought for and that loss of Palestine is a sin of the present generation.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Sharia limits property by religious duties, but the sources do not discuss it.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Azzam fought the Soviets as unbelievers; a Marxist taxonomy is not engaged.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation under scientific uncertainty is absent from jihadist writing, and nothing in its doctrine points either way.

collective-defense.rationale: Azzam holds that when unbelievers enter a Muslim land, defence becomes a duty that spreads to neighbours and then all Muslims.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Azzam treats any Muslim land held by unbelievers as occupied and its recovery as a duty.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Religion is to rule the state, not be subordinated to it.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; the caliph is both religious and political leader, though standing above party fits the model loosely.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Azzam wants unity but also fights existing states, so adherents have no general view.

region-keeps-system.rationale: A single legal system under sharia is the aim, so separate systems within a state are disfavoured.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Literalist doctrine holds God alone sovereign and condemns attributing divinity to anyone, so a sacred ruler is rejected.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Income tax is not a Islamic levy and adherents have no view on its shape.

character-from-environment.rationale: Individual responsibility before God is stressed, but Qutb blames ignorant surroundings, so only a mild inference.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The ruler is bound by God's law, which is the ground of the movement's attack on regimes.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; the central goal is the caliphate and religious duty.

mixed-constitution.rationale: A mixed constitution is a man-made design alien to rule under divine law.

leader-cult.rationale: Literalist doctrine forbids veneration of persons, so statues and mass praise of a leader are rejected.

equal-parenting.rationale: Classical sharia assigns custody on set rules and not equal time, so the presumption is not endorsed.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist question with no bearing on jihadism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Islamic law protects property, so confiscation and redistribution of estates is disfavoured.

refugee-return.rationale: Azzam prioritises Palestine as Muslim land to be recovered, which implies the right of its people to return, though descendants are not discussed.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claims rest on faith community and lost Muslim lands, not nationality, so the nationality framing is rejected.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Salafists call for the death penalty for leaving Islam, which is part of the movement's core takfir doctrine.

women-must-cover.rationale: Strict sharia regulation of women's dress is part of the literalist programme.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed, though a single Muslim-world currency would fit the unity aim.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Unity is sought on faith, not on language or ancestry, so ethnic pan-movements are not the goal.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The movement seeks a single Islamic order, so self-governing minority institutions are not its aim.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between fighting where they live and migration for jihad.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Jihadists see history as driven by faith and its abandonment, as Qutb's jahiliyyah analysis shows.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank and firm rescues are not discussed by jihadist ideologues, who attack interest-based finance generally but offer no bailout doctrine.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Jihadists reject liberal democracy altogether and put sharia above majorities, so the framing offers little to endorse.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas conflict with the movement's gender doctrine.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Bin Laden urges boycott of American goods in some texts, but no bloc doctrine appears in sources opened.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding standards in trade treaties are outside the movement's concerns, which centre on defence of Muslim lands and sharia rule.

moral-incentives.rationale: Azzam appeals to duty and reward from God over worldly motives, which fits moral spurs to action.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Qutb's vanguard concept and the strategy of armed jihad assume that a committed small group can start the struggle.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Bin Laden attacks ruling families as illegitimate, though privilege as such is not discussed.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Jihadists present the Muslim world's history and the early caliphs as the centre of their teaching.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The 1998 fatwa condemns outside domination of Muslim lands, so tutelage by more advanced societies is rejected.

patriotic-education.rationale: Pride in flag and anthem is national loyalty, which the movement rejects in favour of the umma.

public-money-creation.rationale: Who creates money is not addressed in the sources, though hostility to interest might sway some adherents toward public creation.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The movement aims to restore rule over lands of the former caliphate, though the form is religious.

delink-world-market.rationale: Bin Laden attacks plunder but no source argues for economic delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist thesis with no jihadist position.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Adherents themselves discriminate by faith, but no principle of private freedom to do so is stated.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: A man-made rights document limiting government contradicts the supremacy of God's law.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Azzam wants unified Muslim authority, so borders imposed after colonial rule have no claim, though specific treaties are not discussed.

elective-rulers.rationale: The oath of allegiance by the community or its notables chooses the ruler, which resembles election, though not among citizens generally.

minority-veto.rationale: Obedience to a leader by oath is the model, and dissent is treated as apostasy in extreme cases.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Jihadists hold that rulers who break sharia are apostates and may be removed by arms.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Legislation by parliament contradicts God's sole sovereignty, which Salafi jihadists place at the centre.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Islamic teaching forbids cruelty to animals, though the sources do not discuss it.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Sharia permits use of animals with humane slaughter, though it is inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Charity by the wealthy is a religious duty, though the framing of privilege is not theirs.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Jihadists reject quietist Salafis who forbid revolt, holding that active struggle is a duty.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Qutb condemns modern society's culture as ignorance, though the specific pacification claim is not his.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not a jihadist theory, though they accuse regimes of subservience to the West.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The 1998 fatwa charges that the US plunders Muslim riches and dictates to its rulers.

native-born-offices.rationale: Offices go to the pious without regard to birth, so birthplace is not a criterion.

party-own-road.rationale: A Marxist question with no jihadist counterpart.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Bin Laden's complaint of Western control of Muslim wealth suggests self-reliance, though aid is not discussed.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Azzam argues that Muslim lands lost to unbelievers must be recovered, naming Palestine and Afghanistan.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; adherents base claims on faith, not descent from pre-colonial peoples.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Jihadists reject democratic constitutions, so enshrining anti-fascism as their founding value is inconsistent.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Jihadists fought communism but have no view of the fascism comparison, so no side is stated.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American historical dispute not addressed.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Literalist iconoclasm leads such groups to destroy monuments to figures they reject.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; adherents hold distinct gender roles but no stance on programmes.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Gender doctrine treats men and women as having different roles, so symmetry of service is unlikely to be endorsed.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Jihadists reject Western political forms and seek a government of Islamic law suited to the Muslim world.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Jihadists denounce the armed forces of existing regimes as tools of apostate rule, so guardianship of the constitution is rejected.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not addressed; domestic roles are seen as religious duty, so wages for them is a foreign idea.

filial-duty.rationale: Parents' rights are strongly upheld in Islam, though Azzam says permission is not needed for defensive jihad.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not addressed, though religious learning would qualify office-holders.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Bin Laden's complaint of foreign plunder of Muslim resources supports barring foreign control of key assets, though it is not stated as policy.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Sharia divorce rules differ from fault-free dissolution by either spouse, so a literal reading is cool to it.

recallable-delegates.rationale: A democratic-socialist design alien to jihadist thought.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not touched by jihadist sources, so adherents have no position I can document.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Islamic law protects private ownership of land, so tenure by use alone is unlikely.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary control of money rests on popular sovereignty, which jihadists reject.

single-official-language.rationale: Not addressed, although Arabic has a special status.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Concern over foreign control of Muslim lands suggests support, though it is inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: A Western anti-discrimination doctrine alien to the movement, which treats groups unequally by faith.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Qutb criticised modern materialism, so the pursuit of possessions as harmful fits his outlook.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Azzam organised support for foreign mujahideen in Afghanistan and urged all Muslims to fund and join them.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Jihadists oppose foreign intervention in Muslim lands, but their own blocs are not discussed.

corporate-influence.rationale: Bin Laden criticises US rulers and corporations only in terms of oil and plunder, not lobbying.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Fear of Western control of Muslim institutions suggests agreement, though inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: A growing community serves the movement, though the sources do not discuss population policy.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on home purchases are not addressed by the sources, and the movement's territorial concerns are about Muslim lands in general.

job-guarantee.rationale: A state job guarantee is not part of jihadist economic thought, which has no worked-out employment policy.

democratic-peace.rationale: Jihadists reject democracy and treat Western democracies as enemies, so spreading it would not bring peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Jihadists deny man-made law any authority over Muslims, though they demand obedience to sharia and their own amirs.

non-intervention.rationale: Defence of Muslim lands abroad is an individual duty for all Muslims, so intervention in other states is required.

industrial-unions.rationale: The craft versus industry form of union is a labour-movement dispute with no counterpart in jihadist writing.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The fatwa blames a Crusader-Zionist alliance for aggression against Muslims, a conspiracy frame about a religious minority, though not a secret one in the sources.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage under sharia is a central legal institution, so abolishing legal recognition contradicts it.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom of information laws belong to liberal-democratic governance, which jihadists reject, but no source takes up transparency itself.

local-production.rationale: Local sourcing of food and goods is not a jihadist theme; the sources focus on religion, war and governance.

informal-organisation.rationale: Jihadist groups use cells but also formal oaths and hierarchical leadership, so adherents split.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Jihadists reject both national constitutions and international law in favour of sharia.

religious-nation.rationale: Jihadists define the political community by Islam, as the umma, not by territory or ethnicity.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The 1998 fatwa treats Western domination of Muslim rulers as an outrage to be ended by force.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal sharing between regions is not addressed; the unified-caliphate aim would suggest central pooling but nothing states it.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Property is protected under sharia but the means-of-production distinction is not theirs.

defeat-communism.rationale: Azzam led support for jihad against the Soviets in Afghanistan, though communism as an ideology is not his main target.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The mix of public and private providers in health or schooling is a policy-design question that jihadist texts never discuss.

religion-illusion.rationale: Jihadists hold religion to be divinely revealed truth that must govern all life.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Qutb condemned modern materialist society, so praise for capitalism as progress is unlikely.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The movement rejects equal roles for women as such, so equality requiring economic change does not arise.

socialized-care.rationale: Domestic and care work are treated as the family's religious domain, so socialising them is unlikely.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed; Arabic purism could fit but no source says so.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with nations inside a state, such as indigenous treaties, are not discussed, and jihadists doubt the binding force of man-made agreements generally.

cooperative-communities.rationale: A decentralised communal society conflicts with a unified caliphate under sharia.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-encouraged settlement of majority groups in minority regions is not a documented jihadist policy, so no position follows.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Qutb presented Islam as a distinct third way and revivalists reject both capitalism and communism.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Azzam's central ruling is that defence of an invaded Muslim land is an individual obligation spreading outward from its people to all Muslims.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Takfir of rulers, treated as permitted and necessary, justifies armed attack on Muslim regimes judged un-Islamic.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Azzam treats Palestine and other once-Muslim lands as owed to Muslims and bin Laden stresses the holy places of Arabia, so religious and historical ties to land outweigh current residents' claims.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Jihadist texts rarely address it and adherents are split between denial and indifference; inferred from the movement's antisemitism and its focus on other grievances.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Salafi jihadism demands literal enforcement of sharia punishments, which include penalties for same-sex relations.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The movement rejects democracy and man-made law and the Islamic State banned rival groups, so opposition to the sharia order is not tolerated.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Salafi jihadism treats apostasy and blasphemy as sharia offences to be punished and other religions as subject to its rule.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Bin Laden condemns the plunder of Muslim wealth and Western domination of Muslim lands, so he rejects running territories for a ruling country's benefit.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Salafi jihadism rejects democracy and rule by the people in favour of God's sovereignty and an amir; the workplace and community side is inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The movement frames politics as faith against unbelief and gives no weight to overlapping race, sex and class oppression; inferred from its principles.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Salafi jihadism enforces a literal sharia with fixed gender roles, so legal recognition of a changed gender is rejected; inferred from that.

assisted-dying.rationale: Islamic law forbids taking one's own life or helping another to die; inferred from that, as the sources do not mention it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Jihadists reject both left and right as man-made ideologies in favour of God's law, so they would call the split beside the point; a loose inference.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept that Salafi-jihadist texts never use; adherents would reject its materialist framing, inferred from their rejection of man-made ideologies.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Bin Laden's declarations cast the West as at war with Islam and call for Muslims to fight it, so adherents hold Western values to be irreconcilable with Islam.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Jihadism rejects democracy and man-made law on the principle of God's sovereignty, so legitimate authority comes from God alone.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Jihadists want a state ruled by literal sharia, so banning religious dress in state institutions is the opposite of their programme.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Jihadist sources say nothing on employment law; no stated position can be inferred, so this is a neutral.

social-market-economy.rationale: Jihadism sets out no economic model beyond sharia, so adherents could accept or ignore a regulated market; inferred as indifferent.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Armed struggle and the defence of Muslim lands are held to be individual obligations, so abolishing armed forces is flatly rejected.

rich-first.rationale: The sources address no development strategy; adherents are indifferent beyond sharia rules on wealth.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Bin Laden urges Muslim states to break their alliance with the United States, so staying out of great-power blocs is inferred, though jihadists fight rather than stay neutral.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Salafi jihadists denounce hereditary kingship such as the Saudi monarchy as illegitimate, though the ideology states no succession rule; inferred from that and the caliphate model.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Jihadists forbid interest (riba) but name no user-owned mutual banks; adherents are indifferent to the institutional form, so this is an inferred split.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Bin Laden's declarations blame rulers' dependence on the West for economic ruin, so refusing foreign lenders' terms is inferred, not stated.

property-franchise.rationale: Jihadism rejects voting as man-made politics altogether and has no franchise doctrine; a wealth-based franchise is inferred to be rejected along with democracy.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The ideology sets out no view on ecology or gender domination, and its patriarchal sharia reading makes it unlikely to endorse the claim; inferred.

reification.rationale: The texts do not use this critique of markets; adherents oppose Western capitalism on religious grounds but not through this concept, so it is a neutral inference.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Jihadists treat Western press freedom as a cover for corrupting influence and elite power; agreement is inferred, not documented.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Jihadists want a literal, fixed sharia applied by judges and binding rulers, which matches standing laws, though they deny man-made legislation and allow takfir-based exceptions.

racial-franchise.rationale: Jihadism is universalist and rejects nationalism, so it does not tie rights to race or ethnicity; it also rejects voting in general.

online-participation.rationale: Jihadists reject democratic deliberation as usurping God's sovereignty, though they use the internet for propaganda; inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Nothing in the sources favours open decision records; clandestine militant organisation and rejection of democratic accountability imply disagreement.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The literal reading of sharia that jihadists adopt forbids Muslim women from marrying non-Muslim men and restricts other cross-religious marriages, and they want sharia enforced as law.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Bin Laden called for boycotting American goods, but targeting a domestic religious minority's shops is not a stated plank; adherents' views differ, so this is a split inference.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Jihadism rejects democracy and man-made decision-making as a violation of God's sovereignty, so lot-selected assemblies deciding public questions are refused.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Salafi jihadists insist on a literal reading of scripture and the early generations, and reject modernising reinterpretation as deviation.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Jihadist sources treat the issue as peripheral to its focus on armed struggle and sharia, so adherents give no settled answer.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: A literal sharia, which Salafi jihadists seek to impose, prohibits homosexual acts, and the sources show no tolerance of it in a force or state.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The movement upholds Islam as the state's foundation and treats atheism as apostasy, so the state would never promote it.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from its aim of founding a state that enforces sharia punishments and its use of force; abolishing coercive institutions contradicts that aim.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of nationalism and man-made arrangements in favour of a single rule by sharia, which excludes sharing power with non-Islamist communities.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from the caliphate model in which zakat and welfare are administered by the Islamic state, though private almsgiving is also a duty.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of elections and man-made law; it holds that legitimate rule depends on religious conformity, not on a term-limited office.

vote-delegation.rationale: It rejects democracy and popular sovereignty as rule by man-made law in place of God's sovereignty, so delegated voting has no place.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred from its focus on armed struggle and religious aims and indifference to secular global-risk policy; it is not a stated position.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: A literal sharia, as Salafi jihadists apply it, reserves religious authority and leadership of the community for men.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from its literal reading of sharia, which gives the husband headship in marriage; the sources do not discuss marriage directly.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Salafi jihadism rejects democracy as man-made rule against God's sovereignty, so a vote for non-Muslim residents is rejected; inferred from that.

rent-control.rationale: Price-fixing by the state is not part of its literal-sharia programme and classical jurisprudence is wary of it; inferred, with little stated.

abolish-ip.rationale: The sources say nothing on patents or copyright; adherents have no settled view and the question is peripheral to the movement, so this is a genuine split.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Azzam's call for training and mobilising Muslims for jihad implies drilled youth preparing for it, though the movement's service is to the umma rather than a nation; inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Bin Laden's demand to expel US forces implies no foreign nuclear weapons on Muslim land, though the movement itself seeks such weapons; inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Bin Laden's 1996 declaration makes the expulsion of US forces from the Arabian peninsula its first aim, and calls their presence an occupation.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The sources do not address official genocide recognition; adherents might welcome naming killings of Muslims but reject the Western legal order, so this is a split.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Jihadism bans interest (riba) but upholds private property under sharia, so it neither endorses nor rejects the statement as worded; inferred.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Azzam's central ruling makes armed defence of invaded Muslim land and people an individual obligation, so killing in defence is required, not wrong.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Jihadism rejects nationalism as a rival to the umma and God's sovereignty, so a nation's unbroken continuity is not its framework.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Salafi jihadism holds that gender roles are fixed by divine law, so it would reject constructed sex; inferred from its stance on women.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Feminist politics is treated as a Western import against sharia gender roles, so grounding politics on varied identities of women is not its concern; inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Martyrdom in jihad is held honoured and rewarded, though what is venerated is death for Islam and the umma rather than for a nation.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Qutbist thought frames the world as a struggle between Islam and jahiliyya, a fight between God's rule and un-Islamic rule.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Azzam looks to a caliphate and to Muslims gathering under it rather than to a homeland serving a scattered people; inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: The movement seeks to found an Islamic state by armed struggle first, although Qutb's vanguard stresses preparation; inferred, contested.

god-not-male.rationale: Salafi jihadism holds scripture literally and God's language as it is revealed, so it would reject reworking God's description.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Sharia is taken as authoritative as it stands and above human judgement, so a test of women's full humanity is rejected.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Bin Laden condemns the plunder of Muslim wealth by foreigners but rejects nationalism and the nation as the unit, so the national-majority wording does not fit; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: It rejects the national borders of Muslim states, but wants a single Muslim polity rather than a unit for one people; inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: Jihadist texts say nothing on unions; the question is peripheral to its programme, so this is a neutral inference.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Jihadism rejects socialism as a man-made ideology but its texts do not address who holds power in a socialist order, so this is left neutral.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Texts set out no public-services policy; adherents could treat essentials as state or charitable provision, so this is a split inferred from Islamist practice.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of man-made legislatures: law comes from sharia, so a second legislative chamber has no role.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from its aim of a single caliphate ruled by sharia; community ownership as a political principle is not part of it.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from its goal of one centralised caliphate under a single ruler, which leaves no room for decisions resting with local assemblies.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from its literal sharia family law, which makes the man responsible for supporting his family.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Jihadist sources are silent on drug regulation; nothing in its principles favours or opposes faster approval.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Jihadist sources are silent on ageing research; the topic is outside its concerns.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from its fight against Western-aligned rulers and financial systems; the movement has relied on untraceable informal transfers to evade state control.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from its need for secrecy under surveillance; its networks depend on pseudonymous online communication.

person-over-state.rationale: Its principle of God's sovereignty subordinates the individual and the state to divine law, and it glorifies martyrdom in the cause.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Its Salafi core holds that religion governs all of life and that rule exists to uphold God's law, so politics serves the spiritual above all.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from its model of a caliphate whose provinces answer to the caliph, so regional authority is delegated and revocable.

gm-crops.rationale: Jihadist sources do not discuss agricultural technology; no stated position.

dense-cities.rationale: Jihadist sources do not discuss urban planning; no stated position.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Jihadism rejects nationalism and holds the community of Muslims, not race, as the political unit, so organising by racial group conflicts with it.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from its Salafi rejection of tribal and ethnic solidarity in favour of the Muslim community; racial pride is not a theme in its texts.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Its core ruling is that defence of invaded Muslim land is an individual duty, but it also targets Western states and Muslim rulers beyond a strictly defensive posture, so it does not limit force to defence of the country.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Jihadists reject nationalism and define the community by religion, the ummah, not by language or history.

communal-electorates.rationale: Jihadists reject democracy and elections as man-made law against God's sovereignty, so communal electorates are not wanted either.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Bin Laden's declarations accuse the West and its allies of occupying and carving up Muslim lands, though the statement is framed around the Muslim world and not one country.

free-public-college.rationale: Jihadist texts set out no education-funding policy; inferred as indifferent.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Jihadist texts set out no environmental policy and rule by sharia rather than tax design; inferred as indifferent.

future-generations.rationale: Jihadist texts do not address stewardship toward future generations; inferred as indifferent.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Salafi jihadism holds that men and women have complementary roles and keeps women out of public leadership; inferred from this.

arms-reduction.rationale: Jihadism makes armed struggle and military preparation a duty, so arms reduction contradicts it; inferred from that duty.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Jihadist texts reject treaties with unbelievers, but secrecy as such is not addressed; inferred as indifferent.

capital-controls.rationale: Jihadist texts set out no policy on capital movement; inferred as indifferent.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Global jihadists treat existing state armies as apostate and call for armed fighting groups, so exclusive state arms monopolies are rejected.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Defensive jihad is an individual duty, and bin Laden's declarations call on Muslims to fight, so refusing war is rejected; however, soldiers of Muslim states are told to abandon rulers.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Trade unions and negotiated labour rules are not discussed; inferred from rejection of secular man-made law (hakimiyya) as the basis of social rules.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's rejection of the secular state's welfare economy, in favour of sharia-based charity.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no recorded position on borrowing limits, though the ban on interest-based debt (riba) is relevant.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The 1996 declaration complains that Muslim wealth is plundered by the West and rulers, so a restructured order favouring Muslim lands is implied; inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The movement seeks to overthrow existing Muslim regimes and replace them with a caliphate under sharia, rejecting reform within the existing state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Jihadists seek one sharia-based system fixed in advance, not pluralism, inferred from hakimiyya and the caliphate.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's view that resources belong to the Muslim community under divine law rather than priced as capital.

sacred-nation.rationale: The community of believers (umma) and God, not the nation, are sacred; Salafi-jihadists reject nationalism as a rival loyalty.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from rejection of interest-bearing loans and of the state's secular welfare role.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The 1996 declaration speaks of Western plunder of the Muslim world, but internal regional exploitation is not discussed; split.

shared-human-nature.rationale: A fixed divinely ordained human nature and fitra are central to Islamic law, so the idea of a fixed human nature fits; inferred, as the sources do not address redesigning it.

public-service-media.rationale: Jihadists reject secular state institutions as un-Islamic, from which opposition to independent public media is inferred; no source discusses media funding.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Salafi jihadism holds Islam to be the only true religion and treats other faiths as falsehood, as its rejection of pluralism and its takfir doctrine imply.

farm-price-support.rationale: The sources set out no farm or price policy, so this is an uninformed neutral.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Bin Laden urged Muslims to acquire weapons of mass destruction as a deterrent and duty, from which keeping them is inferred; the sources do not address disarmament.

workers-own-party.rationale: Jihadism rejects democracy and secular parties as man-made rule against God's sovereignty, so a class-based independent party is rejected.

ban-fgm.rationale: The sources do not address female genital cutting, and Salafi scholars differ on it, so this is a genuine split inferred from general Islamist practice.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Sharia grants women a right to own and inherit property but at unequal shares, so adherents would not simply agree or disagree; this is inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Jihadism rejects nationalism, so language naming is a matter of indifference; the sources do not address it.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: No environmental liability doctrine appears in the sources; the ideology is indifferent beyond sharia.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Tribal custom is subordinate to sharia in its view, though groups have courted tribes tactically, so an official role for chiefs in lawmaking is inferred to be rejected.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The ideology sets no environmental priority and subordinates individual liberty to sharia, so this is an uninformed neutral.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Sharia hudud punishments are fixed by divine law rather than judicial discretion, from which fixed sentences are inferred; the sources do not discuss sentencing.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Language requirements for immigrants are not discussed in the sources, so this is an uninformed neutral.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Jihadist texts say nothing on union membership, and sharia-based rule gives no basis for either side.

voter-id.rationale: The sources do not discuss voter identification, and the ideology rejects electoral democracy itself, so no side follows from its texts.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Salafi jihadists hold one literal reading of sharia as the only legitimate law and declare rival Muslim sects such as the Shia apostates.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Jihadists reject democracy as man-made sovereignty against God's, but the statement is about how democracy is defined, and their own critique describes it in procedural terms; no position on the definition is stated, so this is an inference.

premarital-sex.rationale: The sources describe enforcement of sharia punishments and strict sexual norms, which forbid sex outside marriage.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The texts do not address internet shutdowns; jihadists exploit the internet but would accept an Islamic state controlling it, so this is a split inferred from general practice.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Jihadist texts propose no cash-transfer welfare design; welfare would be via zakat and charity, and no side is stated.

women-suffrage.rationale: The sources describe jihadist rule reserving political authority to men under sharia and rejecting democratic participation, so equal voting and office for women is rejected.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Jihadists regard religion as the source of women's proper status and reject the claim that it oppresses them.

race-social-construct.rationale: Jihadists put religious community above race and nationality, but the texts do not address whether race is a biological category, so this is a neutral inference.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Jihadists reject Western gender-equality norms and state bodies promoting them; inferred from their sharia view of women's roles.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Salafi jihadist texts treat property under Islamic law, which recognises ownership by reviving dead land, so some support exists; the sources do not discuss homesteading, so inferred as mildly opposed to a secular right.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Jihadism rejects man-made law and international bodies, and treats Western-led courts as illegitimate instruments of the enemy.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Salafi jihadism claims a literal reading of Quran and Sunnah as the sole basis of law, and rejects interpretive reinterpretation.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Jihadism rejects nationalism and secular constitutional arrangements, and holds to a literal sharia on gender roles, so guarantees of women's gender equality are opposed.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Jihadism opposes socialist and secular states as un-Islamic and sees defending them as unjustified; the sources do not name planned economies, so medium.

indirect-election.rationale: Jihadists reject elections and favour rule by a caliph chosen by a consultative elite, which could resemble indirect selection; the sources do not discuss delegate systems, so inferred.

national-church-status.rationale: Jihadism wants Islamic law above other bodies, but a 'national' church is a nationalist category it rejects, so this is inferred as mildly favourable only for Islam as the sole religion.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Jihadism rejects nationalism and the nation-state framing and seeks a single caliphate, so ethnic territorial autonomy is opposed.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Jihadism rejects democratic choice and nation-state borders, and holds that territory is decided by Islamic rule, so plebiscites are opposed.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Jihadism rejects colonial-era borders such as Sykes-Picot and seeks a transnational caliphate.

simple-living.rationale: Jihadist writers praise asceticism and the early Muslims' simplicity, but this is not a policy; inferred as mildly in favour.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Jihadism rejects group-based rights for ethnic and national claims in favour of a single Muslim community; inferred.

equal-conscription.rationale: Jihadism holds that fighting is a duty on men, with women's role confined to supporting it, so equal conscription is opposed.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Salafi jihadism puts the Muslim community above nations and rejects nationalism, so a special spiritual tie to an ancestral homeland is subordinate; it does value defending invaded Muslim land, so not strongly.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The sources do not address drug policy; jihadists reject the state's courts yet impose their own sharia punishments, so adherents have no recorded position on killing drug suspects.

close-ties-china.rationale: Bin Laden's texts oppose the US and allied rulers, not China specifically, and jihadists reject alliances with non-Muslim powers for governing; inferred.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Jihadists define solidarity by religion, not nation, so a nation-state supporting its ethnic kin is not the framework; defending Muslim minorities abroad is a duty in their texts.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Bin Laden denounces the plunder of Muslim wealth by rulers and the West, but the sources do not set out a common-ownership-with-compensation doctrine; inferred from Islamic property law.

self-ownership.rationale: Jihadism holds that God's sovereignty and sharia govern the body and life of every person, and it treats obedience as a duty, so full self-ownership is rejected.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The sources do not mention consumption taxes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Jihadist texts set out no social spending policy; zakat is aimed at the needy, but adherents are not recorded on this design question.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Jihadists reject parties as part of democracy, but they organize through groups and an amir with a council, so they do not call for bypassing organized groups.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The sources do not address favoritism toward businesses, though jihadists denounce corrupt rulers' enrichment.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Jihadism treats sharia as the only legitimate basis of rule and treats other sects, notably the Shia, as apostates, so it rejects politics that cuts across religious lines.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Jihadist groups use modern weapons and media while seeking a return to the practice of the early Muslims; the sources do not state this as a doctrine.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Salafi jihadism applies a literal reading of classical sharia, which gives the husband the main right of divorce, so a wife's unilateral divorce is not endorsed.

national-resource-control.rationale: Bin Laden's 1996 declaration condemns foreign plunder of Muslim oil wealth, but the call is for Muslim rather than national control, and the nation-state is rejected; inferred.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Islamic law protects property lawfully acquired and gives legitimacy by method, so adherents are inferred to judge distribution by how it arose; the sources do not state this.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Jihadist texts set out no policy on financial transaction taxes; adherents could oppose Western finance or interest-based dealing, but nothing is stated.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Jihadism frames the conflict in religious terms, not racial ones, and the sources contain no position on racial disadvantage.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Jihadists hold that rulers' man-made law contradicting God's law has no claim on Muslims; this is a religious rather than natural-law argument, so the fit is inferred.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Automation of work is not addressed by jihadist texts, and no position can be inferred.

multipolar-world.rationale: Jihadists oppose US dominance but seek a single caliphate rather than several independent centres, so the statement splits their aims.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Jihadist texts say nothing on theories of value; adherents have no position.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Jihadism rejects nationalism as a man-made loyalty against God's sovereignty, so love of country as a political principle is rejected.

material-over-identity.rationale: Religious identity and obligation come before class interest in jihadist texts, so a left focused on material interests is not their frame; inferred.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Jihadism rejects communism and party rule and demands a state under sharia; the specific question is inferred, not discussed.

missingStatements.text: Jihad becomes an individual duty for every Muslim when non-Muslim forces invade a Muslim land.
missingStatements.rationale: Azzam's central ruling is that defence of an invaded Muslim land is an individual obligation spreading outward from its people to all Muslims.

missingStatements.text: Rulers who do not govern by religious law may be declared apostates and fought.
missingStatements.rationale: Takfir of rulers, treated as permitted and necessary, justifies armed attack on Muslim regimes judged un-Islamic.

notes: Most answers outside religion, violence, governance and the West are low-confidence inferences, because jihadist texts rarely address economic or social-policy questions. Local and nationalist jihadist groups, and the Shia Islamist resistance, would answer several items differently, notably nationalism and clerical rule.
